why:
installs one launch `from -> to` name remap for one `(name, namespace)` in the executor's fixed remap table (`MAX_REMAPS`). It is the AUTHORITATIVE tier: the generated entry projects the launch file's `<remap>` rules through it. rclrs has no such call -- its remaps arrive only as `--ros-args -r from:=to` on the command line, parsed inside `Context::new`. See `cpp:remove_ros_arguments`.

phase-467 Row 11 follow-through (2026-10-03) -- CORRECTED. This row said rclrs's command-line remaps were something "no image has", so launch was the only channel. Since #1591 a hosted build parses `--ros-args -r` too (`nros::init_with_args` / `nros::Context::new`, through `nros_node::ros_args`), and `Context::create_executor{,_in}` installs those rules in this SAME table tagged `RemapTier::Argv`. They are the FALLBACK: resolution reads the two tiers through `nros_node::names::resolve_name_layered`, so an argv rule loses to a launch rule declared here whatever order the two were installed in -- the local-over-global arrangement rcl has (`rcl_remap_topic_name`, Humble `rcl/remap.h`). Still `extension`: the authoritative tier is launch's, and upstream exposes no call to declare one.

issue 1971 / RFC-0107 step 1 (2026-10-19) -- the generated entry NO LONGER declares through this call. The launch file's `<remap>` rules are one `static const` table in flash the entry installs once, before any tier is set up (`nros_cpp_set_launch_remaps`, `nros_node::set_launch_remaps`), and every executor reads it (`rust:Executor::set_launch_remaps`). This call writes the executor's RUNTIME table (`NROS_EXECUTOR_RUNTIME_REMAPS` slots, 16 with argv, 0 on bare metal), still the authoritative tier, for hand-written callers; at 0 slots it is refused by name (`RemapRefused::NoRuntimeTable`).
